recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-6785 unless a future vocabulary work group decision changes the guidance for multi-code-system value sets.
issue_request: FHIR-6785 was a Published FHIR-core ValueSet change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for DSTU1, asking for a best-practice note that value sets crossing code systems should be created with care to avoid definitional confusion.
initial_application: The issue was applied in SVN revision 5885, visible in git as fa950c848fc680723ebbcd70ea2c13888a0aa292 with subject "#6785 - add note about crossing code systems." That commit added the "Value Sets with multiple code systems" section and the requested best-practice note to source/valueset/valueset-notes.xml; later editorial commits preserved the warning.
additional_context: ValueSet is active in source/fhir.ini, so source/valueset/valueset-notes.xml is in current build scope. The current source still warns that mixing definitional systems can cause confusing, overlapping, and inconsistent definitions. Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no later final decision or community record reversing this guidance.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. No source edit was made because the authoritative current source already implements the Jira resolution.
